arxiv-2301-02496.title: Stealthy Backdoor Attack for Code Models
arxiv-2301-02496.creator: Zhou Yang, Bowen Xu, Jie M. Zhang, Hong Jin Kang, Jieke Shi, Junda He, and David Lo
arxiv-2301-02496.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by Zhou Yang, Bowen Xu, Jie M. Zhang, Hong Jin Kang, Jieke Shi, Junda He, and David Lo. Code models, such as CodeBERT and CodeT5, offer general-purpose representations of code and play a vital role in supporting downstream automated software engineering tasks. Most recently, code models were revealed to be vulnerable to backdoor attacks. A code model that is backdoor-attacked can behave normally on clean examples but will produce pre-defined malicious outputs on examples injected with triggers that activate the backdoors.

arxiv-2309-06229.title: PreciseBugCollector: Extensible, Executable and Precise Bug-fix Collection
arxiv-2309-06229.creator: He Ye, Zimin Chen, Claire Le Goues
arxiv-2309-06229.description: Abstract Bug datasets are vital for enabling deep learning techniques to address software maintenance tasks related to bugs. However, existing bug datasets suffer from precise and scale limitations: they are either small-scale but precise with manual validation or large-scale but imprecise with simple commit message processing.

arxiv-2503-20283.title: A Semi-Lagrangian scheme for Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations with Dirichlet boundary conditions Thanks: 1 Dipartimento di Matematica Guido Castelnuovo, “Sapienza”, Università di Roma, 00185 Rome, Italy (carlini@mat.uniroma1.it). Thanks: 2 Dipartimento di Scienze Economiche, Università degli Studi
arxiv-2503-20283.creator: Elisabetta Carlini 1, Athena Picarelli 2, Francisco J. Silva 3
arxiv-2503-20283.description: Abstract . We study the numerical approximation of time-dependent, possibly degenerate, second-order Hamilton-Jacobi-Bellman equations in bounded domains with nonhomogeneous Dirichlet boundary conditions. It is well known that convergence towards the exact solution of the equation, considered here in the viscosity sense, holds if the scheme is monotone, consistent, and stable.

arxiv-2509-13269.title: A Robust Modular Quantum Processor
arxiv-2509-13269.creator: Ramesh Bhandari
arxiv-2509-13269.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Ramesh Bhandari. We explore the concept of redundancy of critical elements in a quantum computing architecture to circumvent disruption of quantum operations due to a failure of such an element, for example, from a catastrophic cosmic ray event. We illustrate this concept with reference to a recently proposed superconducting modular quantum architecture with a star-like configuration, which has a router at the center that enables superconducting qubit interactions across various modules.

pmc-10670624.creator: Shigeki Yano, Tomokazu Kawaoka, Shintaro Yamasaki, Yusuke Johira, Masanari Kosaka, Yuki Shirane, Ryoichi Miura, Kei Amioka, Kensuke Naruto, Kenji Yamaoka, Yasutoshi Fujii, Shinsuke Uchikawa, Hatsue Fujino, Atsushi Ono, Takashi Nakahara, Eisuke Murakami, Daiki Miki, Masataka Tsuge, Yuji Teraoka, Hiro
pmc-10670624.description: Simple SummaryImmune checkpoint inhibitor therapy has been rapidly developed for the treatment of unresectable hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC). In the IMbrave150 trial, atezolizumab plus bevacizumab was seen as the first-line systemic drug therapy for unresectable HCC because overall survival and progression-free survival were significantly prolonged compared with sorafenib.

pmc-10689383.title: Uterine incarceration: a rare diagnosis in non-pregnant women
pmc-10689383.creator: Laura Tavares Cruz, Catarina Reis-de-Carvalho, Ana Luísa Ribeirinho
pmc-10689383.description: Uterine incarceration (UI) is a rare complication in non-pregnant women. A woman in her 50s presented to the emergency department with acute urinary retention and paresis of the right inferior limb. A neurological exam suggested a decrease in the right lower limb strength.

pmc-10739686.title: Preferences and Perspectives of Black Male Barbershop Patrons on Receiving Health Care in Nontraditional Settings
pmc-10739686.creator: Sarah Chong, Brittany Huynh, Stephanie Wong, Temesgen Woldeyesus, Melvin Faulks, Kenneth El-Amin, Jabari Thibeaux, Joseph Lewis, Robert Harlin, Mario Carter, Ramy Shatara, Crystal Zhou, Akinyemi Oni-Orisan
pmc-10739686.description: Introduction:Non-Hispanic Black men experience a disproportionate rate of morbidity and mortality from hypertension, cardiovascular disease, and other chronic conditions in the United States. Studies have demonstrated the efficacy of community-based health outreach in settings not traditionally utilized for health care.

pmc-10989562.title: Sensitive and high laser damage threshold substrates for surface‐enhanced Raman scattering based on gold and silver nanoparticles
pmc-10989562.creator: Felix Mayr, Robert Zimmerleiter, Patricia M A Farias, Mateusz Bednorz, Yolanda Salinas, André Galembek, Olavo D F Cardozo, Dominik Wielend, Dyego Oliveira, Raquel Milani, Tania M Brito‐Silva, Markus Brandstetter, Eduardo Padrón‐Hernández, Peter Burgholzer, Andreas Stingl, Markus C Scharber, Niyazi S
pmc-10989562.description: Surface‐enhanced Raman scattering (SERS) is a sensitive and fast technique for sensing applications such as chemical trace analysis. However, a successful, high‐throughput practical implementation necessitates the availability of simple‐to‐use and economical SERS substrates. In this work, we present a robust, reproducible, flexible and yet cost‐effective SERS substrate suited for the sensitive detection of analytes at near‐infrared (NIR) excitation wavelengths.

pmc-11355630.title: Mortality Outcomes and Contributing Risk Factors in Patients with Hospital-Associated Disability
pmc-11355630.creator: Soo-Jeong Jo, So-Hee Lee, Hyo-Jin Min, Hee-Ji Kim, Hyun-Ho Kong, Masahiro Kohzuki
pmc-11355630.description: Background/Objectives: Hospital-associated disability (HAD), a functional decline following acute hospitalization, is a common complication associated with mortality and unfavorable prognoses in patients admitted to acute care hospitals. However, few studies have investigated mortality and associated factors in patients with HAD and have been limited by inconsistent HAD assessment tools and criteria.

pmc-11672577.title: A Novel Simulation Model and Training Program for Minimally Invasive Surgery of Hallux Valgus
pmc-11672577.creator: Sergio Morales, Peter Lam, Rebecca Amy Cerrato, Pablo Mococain, Cristian Ruz, Jorge Filippi, Andrés Villa, Julián Varas
pmc-11672577.description: Category:BunionIntroduction/Purpose:Minimally Invasive Surgery (MIS) for Hallux Valgus (HV) has become popular with similar results as open surgery with added benefits such as lower post-operative opioid use and improved cosmesis. However, adopting this technique faces challenges due to a pronounced learning curve.

pmc-13343532.title: Design, synthesis, and biomedical evaluation of Ag/Cu bimetallic MOFs for controlled drug delivery and synergistic therapeutic applications
pmc-13343532.creator: Iqra Saleem, Zia Ul Haq Khan, Ibrahim A. Alsayer, Fida Ullah, Rabia Naz, Mahmood M. S. Abdullah
pmc-13343532.description: Cancer and antibiotic resistance are major global health concerns due to high mortality rates, frequent treatment failures, and the development of resistance to conventional therapies. In the proposed research, a multifunctional silver/copper (Ag/Cu) bimetallic metal–organic framework (MOF) is described as a biomedical platform.
